title: Curation sprint scouting: swimlanes & heuristics (May 2027)
body:
Purpose / quick context:
- Prep doc for Sprint-29 backlog curation workshop (scouting + swimlane definitions).
- Aim: create a repeatable, lightweight ritual for triaging + slicing console + tooling tickets so sprint commitments are predictable.
- This is intentionally pragmatic: cheap rules that reduce decision friction.

Top-level decisions (working):
- Adopt swimlane-first intake: tickets are routed into one primary swimlane on intake (can have secondaries).
- Use a simple 10-point prioritization score (Impact 1-4, Effort 1-3, Risk/Dependencies 1-2) to sort within swimlanes.
- Cutlist rule: if score <= 3 and no customer mention + not on roadmap, surface to "decommit" bucket for next grooming.

Swimlane definitions (scouting notes):
1) Operational / Reliability (Ops)
   - Symptoms: page/alert, SLO regressions, customer-facing failures.
   - Intake cues: pager duty, SRE ticket, customer report.
   - Sprint goal fit: emergency slot + 20% capacity reserved for hotfixes.
2) Revenue & Customer Commitments
   - Symptoms: contract clause, SOW deliverable, renewal blocker.
   - Intake cues: CS flag, AE note in ticket or opp linking.
   - Sprint goal fit: prioritized for dedicated track.
3) Developer Experience (DX) & Onboarding
   - Symptoms: onboarding friction, SDK bugs, console UX that blocks TODO templates.
   - Intake cues: developer feedback thread, onboarding support metrics.
4) Platform Reliability & Perf (infra-facing)
   - Symptoms: queuing/backpressure, cold-starts, regressions in latency.
   - Intake cues: telemetry spike, perf regression alerts.
5) Product Experiments & Explorations
   - Symptoms: prototype, A/B, internal hackday spinoff.
   - Intake cues: PO signoff for experiment; limited timebox.
6) Tech debt / Clean-up
   - Symptoms: TODO in code, rot tickets, refactor proposals.
   - Intake cues: author suggests cost of delay; cross-team impact noted.

Prioritization rubric (scoring, keep simple):
- Impact (1-4): revenue/customer-churn (4), cross-org unblocker (3), UX polish (2), internal nicety (1).
- Effort (1-3): small (<2d)=1, medium (2-7d)=2, large (>7d)=3.
- Risk/Dep (1-2): low=1, high/blocked=2.
- Quick score = Impact - Effort - (Risk-1)  // normalize to 1-10 for sorting. (We'll compute in sheet)

Cut heuristics (for rapid triage during grooming):
- If intake has no customer or roadmap signal AND estimated effort >= 3 AND impact <= 2 => mark for pruning.
- If duplicate-ish to an active epic, link and deprioritize (no new work).
- If feature asks for wide config surface but no usage data -> push to discovery spike (1 week) before commit.

Suggested JQLs / console filters for workshop (draft):
- "project = CONSOLE and status in (Open, 'In Progress') and labels not in (backlog-pruned) ORDER BY priority DESC, created DESC"
- "project = CONSOLE and text ~ "customer:acme""
- Swimlane quick filter: label = swimlane-dx, swimlane-ops, swimlane-revenue, swimlane-platform

Wireframe notes: backlog curation view (one-page prototype)
- Header: sprint selector + capacity slider (set by SRE + Eng leads).
- Left column: swimlane palette (drag ticket into lane). Each lane shows live capacity % and soft budget.
- Middle column: ticket list sorted by quick score with colored pill for cause (customer/reliability/dx). Items can be flagged as 'must ship' or 'decommit'.
- Right column: sprint slices snapshot (capacity used, owner assignments, blockers).
- Inline micro-interactions: quick-assign (typeahead), quick-estimate (1/2/3), add-customer-note (free text), link-PR modal.
- Keyboard shortcuts: j/k to move focus, d to decommit, s to score.

Sprint scouting (capacity and slices)
- Assumptions for Sprint-29 (2-week): team core capacity = 6 FE devs (30 dev-days), 3 BE devs (15 dev-days), 1 SRE (10 dev-days), 10% buffer for bugs/hotfixes.
- Reserve: 2 dev-days per engineer for oncall/overhead. Realistic committed capacity ~ 36 dev-days.
- Suggested allocation: 30% Ops & Hotfix (to reflect platform volatility), 25% Revenue/customer work, 20% DX, 15% Platform perf, 10% Experiments/TD.
- Example slices:
   * Hotfix lane: INF-4879 (pager follow-up) - 4 dev-days - assign: Ibrahim
   * Revenue: INF-4823 (billing export fix) - 6 dev-days - assign: Lina
   * DX: INF-4901 (console onboarding flow) - 5 dev-days - split FE/BE
   * Platform perf spike: INF-4915 (batching regression) - 6 dev-days - SRE lead

Unresolved questions / debate items:
- Should swimlane be single-mapped or multi-tagged? (pros/cons: single simplifies capacity math, multi reflects reality). Leaning single-primary + secondaries.
- How strict is the cutlist? Who can veto? Proposal: product lead + eng manager veto for any decommit on revenue/commitments.
- Scoring automation: add a tiny metadata field on ticket for Impact/Effort/Risk so console can show quick-score; need a small PR to JIRA connector.

Immediate next actions (owner initials):
- Aisha: draft JQLs into a saved board + add swimlane labels (by 2027-05-06).
- Marcus: prototype the backlog curation mock in Figma (basic drag lanes) - due 2027-05-10.
- Lina: run quick metrics check for tickets flagged "DX" last 90 days (usage impact) - due 2027-05-07.
- Ibrahim: triage Ops tickets with oncall summary and surface top 3 must-fix items.

Meeting agenda for grooming workshop (45m):
- 5m: scope + sprint capacity recap
- 10m: swimlane definitions + scoring primer (live demo of scoring)
- 20m: triage top 12 tickets (quick score + assign)
- 5m: create cutlist and finalize sprint slice allocations
- 5m: action items + owners

Notes-to-self / scribbles:
- keep cutlist language gentle: "deferred" > "rejected". We want low friction.
- consider a daily 10-min morning slot during sprint to absorb ops hotfixes without derailing planned work.
- test small automation: when score changes below threshold, auto-add label "backlog-pruned-candidate" and ping product slack.

Referenced tickets (examples):
- INF-4823: Billing export missing conversion rows (revenue-impact)
- INF-4879: Queue stall on blob uploads after kernel change (ops)
- INF-4901: First-time user flow: keypair onboarding (dx)
- INF-4915: Batching perf regression after model switch (platform)

End of doc.

(Informal; will iterate after workshop. Drop comments in the Confluence page linked above or add inline suggestions in this Drive doc.)
